subject: Post-call recap: Dedicated capacity needs & next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@lumenhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-03T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: Dedicated capacity needs & next steps

Hi Laura —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re aligned and can move to a proposal: 

Pain points you shared
- Production latency spikes during peak appointment reminder campaigns (95th percentile > 2.5s).
- Concerns about PHI handling and logical separation across business units.
- Unexpected token cost when model is served on shared endpoints; predictability is important for budgeting.

Goals (90/180 day)
- Get a Dedicated capacity deployment with reserved GPUs for the patient-messaging pipeline within 6–8 weeks.
- Private networking (VPC peering) and customer-managed KMS for encryption-in-transit and at-rest.
- SLA target: 99.9% uptime for the dedicated cluster; P95 latency under 1.0s for short prompt paths.

What Redwood recommends (high level)
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool): 4x A100-equivalent nodes to start (can autoscale for bursts).
- Isolation: single-tenant cluster with VPC peering + KMS integration.
- Cost predictability via monthly committed units and per-token soft caps; we’ll include quantization profile options to reduce unit costs by ~30% with minimal quality impact.

Next steps
1) I’ll send a formal capacity estimate and draft SOW (attached).
2) Marissa (cc) will scope the exact node sizing and expected throughput for your busiest day.
3) If procurement needs anything specific, loop them in — we can share SOC 2 artifacts and a standard SLA appendix.

Attachments: redwood_capacity_estimate_v1.xlsx, DRAFT_SOW_Lumen_v1.pdf

Open items for you
- Confirm target go-live window (you mentioned mid-May) and any blackout dates for rollout.
- Any procurement contact or PO process details we should expect?

Happy to jump on a 20-minute follow-up if useful.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0142

--
Redwood Inference — Make inference predictable and economical

From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@lumenhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, procurement <procurement@lumenhealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-03T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Dedicated capacity needs & next steps

Thanks Ben — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Timeline: mid-May still looks feasible; we need procurement signoff by April 22 to hit that.
- Isolation: VPC peering and customer KMS are must-haves. We also need audit logging for token-level access for compliance.
- Throughput: our busiest campaign expects ~1.2M tokens/hour sustained for a 3-hour window; P95 target of <1.2s.

I can share a procurement checklist — forwarding internal point of contact to procurement@lumenhealth.com (cc’d).

Next: please provide the final estimate and a version of the SOW that includes timelines and a simple onboarding plan. Also include expected lead time for reserved GPU capacity and SLA credit language.

Best,
Laura Chen
Head of Product, Lumen Health
laura.chen@lumenhealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@lumenhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-04T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Dedicated capacity needs & next steps

Laura — great, thanks for the specifics. Quick update attached:

- I’ve updated the capacity estimate (redwood_capacity_estimate_v1.xlsx) to show a starter config of 4x A100-equivalent nodes with autoscale headroom to 8 nodes during bursts; that maps to your 1.2M tokens/hr requirement with P95 headroom.
- Draft SOW now includes: 6-week timeline to provision + onboarding, VPC peering tasks, KMS integration checklist, and SOC 2 artifacts delivery timeline.
- SLA: proposing 99.9% uptime for the dedicated cluster with a simple credits schedule; Marissa will confirm the exact credit percentages and blackout exceptions.

Immediate ask from you: please confirm procurement timeline (April 22) and whether we should include a 60-day termination clause vs. 90-day (we can adjust depending on legal).

If procurement wants, I can set a short call between our contracts lead and your procurement team this week.

Thanks — I’ll put together a concise one-pager for your CFO on predictable monthly spend vs. pay-as-you-go and share it after the call.

Best,
Ben

Attachments: redwood_capacity_estimate_v1.xlsx, DRAFT_SOW_Lumen_v1.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Chen <laura.chen@lumenhealth.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, procurement <procurement@lumenhealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-05T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Dedicated capacity needs & next steps

Looping in operational details from infra:

- Node lead time: for reserved A100-equivalent capacity in our AP/US pools we can provision within 3–4 weeks once the purchase order is approved; AMER region typically 3 weeks.
- Onboarding milestones:
  1) Week 0–1: PO sign + account setup (VPC peering prep).
  2) Week 2–3: Provision cluster + KMS integration + SOC 2 evidence transfer.
  3) Week 4–6: Validation runs, load testing, and cutover plan.

- Observability: we’ll enable token-level traces for the first 30 days on a limited retention window; full retention options are available as an add-on.

I’ll follow up with the exact SLA appendix language and the proposed credit schedule. If procurement can aim for April 22, we should be able to meet mid-May go-live.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
